initial.summary: A QA tutor and three tutors report that LT audio will not play or the player never loads, and ask whether to use QN. Current guidance says to report a technical issue, not infer a content-quality failure from unavailable playback; no repair is confirmed in these threads.
initial.reasoning: The four distinct reporters describe comparable playback failures. Current instructions and the relevant batch reminder already establish handling, so clarification of the QN rule does not need to wait for a technical diagnosis. An engineer and the team lead request diagnostic details, supporting an engineering report that distinguishes known task references from details still needed. The historical reload trial expired and has no observed outcome in the supplied record; it cannot establish that any current reporter tried a workaround or that it failed. Earlier interpretation-review flags remain open.

claims.text: A QA tutor and three tutors report that the LT player never loads or audio will not play, ask whether to use QN, and recall a possible workaround from the previous queue.
A tutor also reports that the waveform loads but pressing Play never starts sound.
claims.quote: The waveform loads but pressing Play never starts sound.

claims.text: Current instructions and the FAQ require reporting unavailable playback as a technical issue with the task ID and available reproduction details. Playback failure alone does not justify a model-quality failure or content-based QN; separate accessible content concerns should be retained for review.

Current instructions and the batch playback reminder call for the browser/error state and whether another clip plays, including when a waveform is visible but playback does not start. Handling instructions do not confirm a repair.
An engineer requests the LT error state and time for tasks AUDIO-2197 and AUDIO-4294 and explicitly says the wider cause is not confirmed in those threads.

In the QA tutor's thread and a tutor's AUDIO-6012 thread, the team lead requests task IDs and a reproduction attempt before deciding whether the old workaround applies. In the QA tutor's thread, the team lead also asks that both task references be kept if another clip plays.

In two tutors' threads, the team lead says the affected task cannot be evaluated while the player fails to load and instructs each thread to report the playback incident with its task ID rather than mark the recording as a model-quality failure.

The earlier batch had an approved, posted trial allowing at most one reload for a player stuck at 00:00 through August 28. The record marks the outcome as not observed and describes the reload as diagnostic, not a confirmed repair; the trial is expired.
Current instructions require checking an old workaround against current symptoms and say recurrence alone does not establish which fix was tried or why it failed.

k:audio-multimodal-faq@1.1:c724358c.excerpt:
## Playback and tool issues

### Q: What if the player spins forever or never loads?
Report the task ID and available reproduction details as a tool incident. Do not score the recording as a model-quality failure while it cannot be evaluated.

### Q: Can I use QN because playback is unavailable?
Playback failure alone does not establish a content-based QN reason. Report the tool incident. If other accessible evidence raises a separate content concern, retain it for review rather than assuming what the unavailable audio contains.

diagnostics.text:
Post a reminder. Instruction: Post a shared handling reminder in the affected threads and direct tutors to collect playback examples in the existing batch thread. Draft to copy: For audio batch 06, a player that never loads or shows a waveform without starting playback should be reported as a tool incident. Include the task ID, browser and error state, error time, reproduction details, and whether another clip plays; keep both task references if one plays and the other does not.

Do not assign a model-quality failure or content QN solely because playback is unavailable. Retain any separate accessible content concerns for review. Please keep examples in the existing batch playback thread while the scope is checked. These handling instructions do not mean playback has been repaired, and the old workaround still needs review before use. Why this helps: A shared reminder can answer the repeated QN question and standardize the details collected. It follows current project and batch guidance, but mostly repeats existing instructions and does not itself advance engineering investigation of the multiple reported failures.
diagnostics.rationale: The technical-incident reminder and diagnostic requirements follow current guidance. However, its listed premises do not establish directing these reporters to the existing batch example-collection thread; the cited collection note is not operational playback-handling guidance.

diagnostics.text: No action needed now. Instruction: Hold a new consolidated escalation until you have reviewed the missing reproduction details and the earlier reload trial's outcome. Draft to copy: No new consolidated escalation yet: I will review the task references and reproduction details, then check the earlier reload trial's results and any later approval before deciding whether it applies. The prior trial was limited to the previous batch and has expired. Continue reporting individual tool incidents under current guidance; do not infer a content failure from unavailable playback. Why this helps: Current thread instructions support gathering details before deciding whether the old workaround applies, and historical records do not establish an extension or observed trial outcome. They do not support delaying current incident reporting, so waiting on a consolidated escalation is a poor fit for the assessed high severity.
diagnostics.rationale: Reviewing diagnostics and trial outcomes before deciding workaround applicability is supported. Holding a consolidated escalation pending that review is not justified by those requirements, and the alternative itself acknowledges the poor fit with the multiple current reports.
